sourceScope: the branch fix/552-canvas-parity branched from this commit; the canvas-parity fix recorded below and this receipt land in the PR, so the next commit that touches source carries them

executionScope.runNote: no flake in this round. Each of the five canvas-parity checks was proved to bite first, one gap at a time, on the same binary build path: the fix was reverted for that gap alone, the suite was rerun and the case failed for that gap, then the fix was restored. Those red runs are recorded per gap under reviewRound.

familyGeometry.test: draws every engine family's boxes, routes and label breaks in WKWebView
asserted: data-engine-geometry-status settles on ready for the opened document
data-engine-spec-sha256 equals the hash of the source spec the fixture laid out
every engine member's box equals the engine's box for that member
the shape actually drawn for a member is measured and equals the engine's box for it within 2 px, so the attribute the canvas writes is not the only evidence
the painted route path equals the engine's route path, compared on the visible stroke path and never on the transparent hit path
every sampled point of a visible route that lands inside a container hit-tests back to that route, so no lane, boundary, stage, segment or activation is painted over a route the engine ran inside it
each engine label carries the engine's wrapped lines, including the mixed Korean and English label
each placed engine label paints its first line within 2 px of the origin of the engine's own label box on both axes, and stays inside that same box within 2 px
the expected label origin and box are the engine layout's, read through fixedToPixels of label.bounds, so a painted label that moved but stayed inside its owner still fails
familyGeometry.containerSampleReading: 521 samples across the five families land inside a container and all of them hit-test back to their own route. Sequence shows 0 because its four routes run outside every container, so it has no sample that a container fill could hide.

enginePrimitives.test: draws the shapes the writer paints but no member covers
asserted: every primitive the engine publishes for a canvas family — a sequence lifeline, a lifecycle initial marker, stem, head, band, rail or final border — is painted, by owner and in the layer the report names
each painted primitive's box equals the engine's own coordinates within 1.5 px, measured from the drawn element rather than from an attribute
a painted primitive takes no pointer, so a lifeline or band never swallows a pan, a marquee or a member drag
legend swatches are the one kind the canvas drops, because it has no legend for them to key, and it paints none of them
the check is not vacuous: at least one non-legend primitive was compared

sequenceLifelines.test: draws a lifeline for every sequence participant
asserted: the engine publishes exactly one sequence lifeline per participant, counted against the scene's own nodes
the canvas paints that many, each at the engine's own x, y and length within 1.5 px
each lifeline starts on its own participant's bottom edge at its centre, so the messages read against the right timeline

pageTitle.test: keeps every page title clear of the members and containers the scene paints
asserted: every page label the engine emitted is painted, with the engine's own lines
every page label is painted after every member and container group in document order, so page chrome sits above the scene
no member or container outline shares more than 2 px² with a page label's drawn box
the check is not vacuous: page labels were compared for all five families, and the fixture's lifecycle family is present

routeLabelBox.test: draws each labelled relation's text inside the box drawn for it
asserted: the box drawn around a route label is the engine's own label box grown by ENGINE_LABEL_BOX_PAD (3 px) on each side, within 2 px
the text stays at least 2 px inside that box on all four sides, so it is never stroked at its own bounds
the check is not vacuous: 9 route labels across the five families were compared

ovalLabel.test: keeps every oval state's label inside the curve it is drawn in
asserted: the canvas draws a lifecycle start, success or failure state as an ellipse, measured from the drawn element
every corner of that state's painted label lies on or inside the drawn ellipse (reach ≤ 1.02 of its radius)
the check is not vacuous: at least one oval carried a label

legacyDocuments.test: reopens v7, v8 and v9 documents without losing content
asserted: each file reports sourceVersion 7, 8 or 9 and migrates to 9
two opens of the same file are equal
the v7 table upgrade mints exactly one dataset, v8 gains none and the v9 semantic document keeps its one
a legacy document paints as many members as the fixture reports nodes and none of them engine-sourced, so it still draws its own placement
every painted member has area and the members paint text

applyUndoRedoReopen.test: applies a structural edit, undoes, redoes and reopens it
applyUndoRedoReopen.reopenRule: no saved field is lost, and a second load adds nothing the first load did not already fill; loader defaults above are what the migration writes, not content the engine dropped

nativeExportReceipts.test: exports SVG and PNG on the native engine path with verified receipts
asserted: both receipts carry a 64-hex output hash
both receipts report readback status passed, a byte comparison by the native host
both written files are non-empty

interaction.test: pans, zooms and selects on the engine scene

refusalDiagnostic.test: anchors the engine's refusal diagnostic beside its element
asserted: the canvas settles on refused and keeps a 64-hex engine spec hash
the badge carries the engine's own code and is anchored to the member the engine named
no unanchored canvas notice appears alongside the anchored diagnostic
the badge's aria-label carries the engine's code and JSON path
the badge's drawn transform equals the placement the same mapper produces from the same document and the same displayed members, so the expectation does not come from the DOM
the badge's drawn box is adjacent to its member (nearest edge within 24 px) but its side is not pinned: which side is free is the mapper's decision
the badge overlaps no other member's box and no other label, measured on drawn client rectangles, while it may cover its own anchor and sit inside a lane frame
the badge stays in the keyboard order (tabIndex 0) and is announced as a note (role="note")

englishUi.test: draws the same scene in the English UI

paintOrder.defect: the canvas painted container fills - lanes, boundaries, stages, segments, activations - after the routes, so an opaque lane rect covered any route the engine ran inside it; the Maru visual SVG emitted the same wrong order
paintOrder.fix: src/components/diagram/canvas/CanvasSurface.tsx paints containers, then routes, then members, and src/lib/diagram/renderSvg.ts emits the same three bands so canvas and export agree
paintOrder.redBeforeFix: on the pre-fix tree the new hit-test failed: architecture: route conn1 is covered at (169.6,110.0) by g data-engine-source-id="boundary:0"
paintOrder.greenAfterFix: this run: 139, 166, 0, 46 and 170 container route samples for architecture, workflow, sequence, dataflow and lifecycle, with no covered route in any family
paintOrder.unitGuard: src/components/diagram/canvas/CanvasSurface.engineGeometry.test.tsx asserts the canvas paint order lane < approve < draft/review and the export order lane < approve < member

labelBaseline.defect: dominant-baseline="text-before-edge" was declared on the <text> element only; WebKit does not inherit it into child <tspan>s, so every engine label painted about one ascent high and straddled its box, while Chromium inherited the value and looked correct
labelBaseline.fix: NodeView EngineLabels, EdgeView EngineRouteLabel and renderSvg's engineLabelsSvg declare the baseline on each tspan, and the canvas and the export apply the same per-line rule
labelBaseline.redBeforeFix: with the paint order fixed and the baseline not, the new label assertion failed: architecture: label title paints its first line at (32.0,-11.8); the engine put it at (32.0,16.0)
labelBaseline.greenAfterFix: this run: every placed engine label of the five families starts within 2 px of the engine's first-line origin and stays inside the box that owns it
labelBaseline.unitGuard: src/components/diagram/canvas/CanvasSurface.engineGeometry.test.tsx asserts a dominant-baseline on every canvas tspan and on every exported tspan
labelBaseline.chromium: Chromium already inherited the text element's value, so declaring it per line leaves a Chromium render where it was

labelOrigin.defect: the label-position assertion was self-referential: the spec read the painted <text> x/y, added the owner's origin, and compared the painted bbox against that number, so a canvas that moved a label while keeping it inside its owner passed the check meant to catch it
labelOrigin.fix: the bridge publishes the engine's own label bounds (fixedToPixels of label.bounds x/y/w/h, the conversion the node boxes already use); the spec compares the painted first line against that origin in canvas coordinates and measures containment against the same engine label box. Nothing in the expectation comes from the DOM.
labelOrigin.redBeforeFix: a local 4 px shift of the painted label origin failed with: architecture: label container:boundary:0:label paints its first line at (186.0,56.0); the engine put the label box at (182,56)
labelOrigin.greenAfterFix: after reverting the shift: 7 passing in the focused run and 7 passing (4.9s) in the suite recorded here
labelOrigin.testSurface: e2e-native/specs/diagram-engine-e4.spec.ts and src/lib/nativeE2eBridge.ts; the spec keeps its own copy of the family type, so both declarations gained the box field

enginePrimitives.defect: the canvas drew members, containers and routes but dropped every shape the writer paints that no member covers — a sequence's lifelines, a lifecycle initial marker, stem, head, band and final border — so a sequence's messages floated with no participant timeline under them
enginePrimitives.fix: one derivation in src/primitives.rs, published as GeometryDocument.primitives in paint order by the layout and consumed by both writers: the canvas through src/components/diagram/canvas/EnginePrimitives.tsx in the underlay and overlay bands CanvasSurface already paints, and the export through enginePrimitivesSvg in src/lib/diagram/renderSvg.ts. Legend swatches stay out of the canvas adapter because it has no legend for them to key.
enginePrimitives.redBeforeFix: with the two <EnginePrimitives> bands removed and everything else in place, the run failed twice: 'sequence: the engine published a sequence-lifeline for api and the canvas painted none; painted []' and 'sequence: the canvas painted 0 of the engine's 3 lifelines'
enginePrimitives.greenAfterFix: this run: 3 of 3 lifelines painted for the three sequence participants, and 4 of 4 lifecycle shapes (final border, initial dot, stem, head), each at the engine's coordinates with pointer-events none
enginePrimitives.unitGuard: src-tauri/crates/maru-diagram-engine/tests/published_primitives.rs holds the report and the SVG against each other, and src/lib/diagram/engineCanvasGeometry.test.ts plus src/components/diagram/canvas/CanvasSurface.engineGeometry.test.tsx cover the adapter and the two bands

pageTitleBand.defect: the lifecycle page title was painted under the lane that frames the scene. Two causes: the engine's emitted header band shifted workflow and dataflow but not lifecycle, so its first row started inside the band, and the canvas painted page chrome before the containers.
pageTitleBand.fix: layout header_shift includes lifecycle, so the drawing moves below the measured band in Korean or multi-line titles too, and both renderers paint page chrome last: CanvasSurface after the overlay band and renderSvg after the members.
pageTitleBand.redBeforeFix: both halves were proved separately. With page chrome painted first again: 'architecture: page label title is painted before a member or container group, so the scene covers it'. With lifecycle dropped from header_shift and the paint order kept: 'lifecycle: page label title is covered by lane:main over 1496.6px²; the title band must stay clear of the scene'
pageTitleBand.greenAfterFix: this run: page labels painted for all five families, each after every member and container group, with no shared area; the lifecycle title's box (32,16,47.046875,36) sits clear of lane:main
pageTitleBand.unitGuard: src-tauri/crates/maru-diagram-engine/tests/lifecycle_band_title_svg.rs pins the shifted geometry and the emitted band, and the T4 label checks in CanvasSurface.engineGeometry.test.tsx keep the page label in the last band

routeLabelBox.defect: a route label's background box was stroked at the engine's measured text bounds, so the text touched its own border and read as cramped against a diagonal route
routeLabelBox.fix: ENGINE_LABEL_BOX_PAD (3 px) grows the drawn box outward in EdgeView and in renderSvg's edge label, and the text origin is left exactly where the engine put it, so the label-origin assertion still holds
routeLabelBox.redBeforeFix: with the pad set back to 0: 'architecture: route label edge:conn1:label draws its box at (161.1,34.0) 37.9x18.0 instead of the engine's label box (161.078125,34,37.859375,18) grown by 3px'
routeLabelBox.greenAfterFix: this run: 9 route labels across the five families draw their box at the engine's label box grown by 3 px on each side, with the text at least 2 px inside on all four sides
routeLabelBox.unitGuard: src/lib/diagram/renderSvg.engineGeometry.test.ts emits the padded box, and src/components/diagram/canvas/CanvasSurface.engineGeometry.test.tsx asserts the canvas draws the same padded rect

ovalLabelPlacement.decision: engine label placement, not a canvas inset. The canvas draws the oval the document asks for and must not move text the engine measured, so a label that crosses the curve is a layout defect.
ovalLabelPlacement.defect: a lifecycle start, success or failure state is drawn as an oval, but its label was placed from the box's own text inset and wrapped to the box's whole width, so the text ran across the curve
ovalLabelPlacement.fix: layout marks those states as ellipses before placing them (SceneBuilder.mark_ellipse from the lifecycle placer) and fits their text inside the ellipse's inscribed rectangle (ELLIPSE_INSET = (1 − 1/√2)/2 per axis). A label that cannot fit that way demotes the node to its full box instead of turning an accepted document into a refusal, and no oval grows to make room.
ovalLabelPlacement.redBeforeFix: with ELLIPSE_INSET set back to 0 and everything else in place: 'lifecycle: label node:queued:label reaches 2.000 of oval queued's radius at (60.0,120.0), so it is painted across the curve'
ovalLabelPlacement.greenAfterFix: this run: both ovals (queued at centre (130,152) radius (70,32) and done at (538,152) radius (70,32)) carry their labels wholly inside the curve
ovalLabelPlacement.unitGuard: the lifecycle layout tests assert the inscribed-rectangle origin and the demotion ladder, and src-tauri/crates/maru-diagram-engine/tests/lifecycle_band_title_svg.rs keeps the emitted label boxes pinned

badgeCollision.closesPreviousFollowUp: the followUps entry of the previous receipt, which recorded the anchored badge overlapping the neighbouring member's label and blocking its pointer
badgeCollision.defect: the anchored refusal badge was drawn at a fixed offset from its anchor at a fixed 300x44 size, so on a packed workflow scene it covered the neighbouring member's label and took that member's click
badgeCollision.fix: the mapper owns the size (CANVAS_DIAGNOSTIC_BADGE) and the placement: right of the anchor first, then above, below, right-and-under, and opposite last, sliding a step at a time and scoring off-page as unreachable, so the badge lands on the first side that covers nothing. It may cover its own anchor and sit inside a lane frame, never another member or label; the renderer draws at exactly the placed box and keeps the badge in the keyboard order.
badgeCollision.redBeforeFix: with placeBadge reduced to the fixed right-side offset: 'the badge covers [{"name":"merge","shared":1915}]; it may hide its own anchor but never another member or label'
badgeCollision.greenAfterFix: this run: the badge sits at (64,20), above its own member and clear of every other member and label, 0 members covered, still tabIndex 0 and role="note"
badgeCollision.unitGuard: src/lib/diagram/canvasDiagnostics.test.ts asserts zero overlap with every drawn box except the badge's own member for all five diagnostic families, and src/components/diagram/canvas/CanvasDiagnostics.test.tsx asserts the drawn size and the keyboard order

screenshots.regenerate: make test-e2e-native rewrites this directory from the run it makes; screenshots.json there is written by the spec's after() hook, so a failing case still leaves its captures

productDefect.classification: harness-surfaced robustness change, not a reproduced product defect
productDefect.found: the canvas gesture handlers called SVGSVGElement.setPointerCapture without a guard
productDefect.whyItSurfaced: the embedded driver dispatches synthetic PointerEvents, and WebKit raises NotFoundError for a pointer id it never activated; unguarded, that throw leaves the handler before it sets its own gesture state
productDefect.notClaimed: no press, pan or marquee was reproduced failing under real OS input on an unguarded build, so this is recorded as robustness the harness asked for rather than a user-visible defect
productDefect.fix: src/components/diagram/canvas/CanvasSurface.tsx capturePointer() attempts capture and ignores a refusal, since losing capture only costs events delivered outside the surface

limits.koreanIme: not covered; WebDriver cannot compose through the macOS input method, so Korean IME composition stays a human check
limits.syntheticPointer: the embedded driver injects synthetic mouse events only (mousedown, never pointerdown) and this WKWebView reports hasFocus() false, so the terminal's first-mouse guard swallows document-level pointerdown; the spec dispatches PointerEvents at the app's handlers and asserts the canvas state they produce, and a synthetic pointer id is also what makes capture refusable
limits.scope: a debug native-e2e build on one macOS host; no notarization, updater or release-binary claim, and Chromium Playwright evidence remains the separate frontend gate
